newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: East Timor talks set for next week at U.N..
newsitem.headline: East Timor talks set for next week at U.N..

text.p: Ambassadorial-level talks between Indonesia and Portugal on the question of East Timor will be held at U.N. headquarters from August 4 to 8, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Wednesday.
They will be chaired by Secretary-General Kofi Annan's special representative for East Timor, Jamsheed Marker, a Pakistani former U.N. representative.

Before the talks get under way, Marker will hold consultations with Annan in New York and then fly to South Africa to confer with President Nelson Mandela, who has offered to assist the United Nations with the problem.

After two days of talks at the United Nations in June, the foreign ministers of Portugal and Indonesia agreed that senior officials of the two sides would embark on intensive negotiations on East Timor, beginning July 28. The date has been postponed one week.

Indonesia occupied East Timor in 1975 after a civil war erupted following Portugal's withdrawal from its colony. In 1976 Indonesia incorporated the territory as its 27th province but this has never been recognised by the United Nations.
U.N.-mediated talks between the foreign minister of Indonesia and Portugal have been continuing since 1983 aimed at finding an internationally acceptable solution to the problem.
